2.w: “This is why my troubled thoughts bring me back — because of my feelings within me.

3.w: When I hear a reproof that dishonors me, then my understanding prompts me to answer.

4.w: “Surely you know that it has been from old, ever since humankind was placed on the earth,

5.w: that the elation of the wicked is brief, the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.

6.w: Even though his stature reaches to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,

7.w: he will perish forever, like his own excrement; those who used to see him will say, ‘Where is he?’

8.w: Like a dream he flies away, never again to be found, and like a vision of the night he is put to flight.

9.w: People who had seen him will not see him again, and the place where he was will recognize him no longer.

10.w: His sons must recompense the poor; his own hands must return his wealth.

11.w: His bones were full of his youthful vigor, but that vigor will lie down with him in the dust.

12.w: “If evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,

13.w: if he retains it for himself and does not let it go, and holds it fast in his mouth,

14.w: his food is turned sour in his stomach; it becomes the venom of serpents within him.

15.w: The wealth that he consumed he vomits up, God will make him throw it out of his stomach.

16.w: He sucks the poison of serpents; the fangs of a viper kill him.

17.w: He will not look on the streams, the rivers that are the torrents of honey and butter.

18.w: He gives back the ill-gotten gain without assimilating it; he will not enjoy the wealth from his commerce.

19.w: For he has oppressed the poor and abandoned them; he has seized a house which he did not build.

20.w: For he knows no satisfaction in his appetite; he does not let anything he desires escape.

21.w: Nothing is left for him to devour; that is why his prosperity does not last.

22.w: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress overtakes him. The full force of misery will come upon him.

23.w: While he is filling his belly, God sends his burning anger against him and rains down his blows upon him.

24.w: If he flees from an iron weapon, then an arrow from a bronze bow pierces him.

25.w: When he pulls it out and it comes out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver, terrors come over him.

26.w: Total darkness waits to receive his treasures; a fire that has not been kindled will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

27.w: The heavens reveal his iniquity; the earth rises up against him.

28.w: A flood will carry off his house, rushing waters on the day of God’s wrath.

29.w: Such is the lot God allots the wicked, and the heritage of his appointment from God.”
